what_would_bite: A consumer records the documented waiver `id = "RULE.CIT.DOI", scope = "policy", target = "*"`. CFG.EXEMPTIONS accepts it (Doctor.jl:340 — the id is in RULES.toml), EXEMPT.STALE passes it (target `*` returns true at Doctor.jl:380), and Sync.deviations (Sync.jl:104) renders it into .gbg/policy/deviations.md as a granted deviation — but Scan.apply_ledger looks the policy entry up under the scalar row["rule"] = RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE only, so nothing matches and the DOI half of the hard scan (doi_crosscheck.jl's `require_doi` branch, "a reference without a DOI or Open Library link on its title") keeps failing the gate: a silently void waiver on the rule whose ONLY declared check is this scan. The mirror case over-reaches: a policy waiver on RULE.CIT.FULL_INLINE disables the whole scan and withdraws RULE.CIT.DOI enforcement the consumer never exempted, while RULES.toml still advertises the scan as catching it. Same shape on SCAN.DEAD_REF (column RULE.DOC.NO_DEAD_REFS; RULE.CIT.NO_INACCESSIBLE unwaivable) and SCAN.API_PAGE_STRUCTURE (column RULE.DOC.INTERNAL_API; RULE.DOC.API_GROUPING waivable for its sibling HTML scans but not this one — the asymmetry). The dismissal's accepted remedy, a scans.toml header telling a READER to consult §12.B instead, does not touch the engine that resolves waivers through the column, and its stated mechanism ("a SCALAR by schema") is not backed by any schema: schema/ holds no scans schema and scan_catalog() is a bare TOML.parsefile of catalog/scans.toml.
